messages:
Ajay K: I need a hand — family emergency, gotta run. I'm primary for the holiday weekend but gotta hand off now. I'll keep my laptop nearby but may be offline for long periods.
ops-schedule-bot: @Ajay K, you're marked as OOO starting now per your calendar. Paging policy engaged for primary fallback.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — service=redwood-runtime region=us-west-2 severity=high — multiple model-worker OOMs detected (5/10 workers failing) — alert: https://redwood.incidents/3771234567
Maria R: On it, taking initial deputy. Ajay — any running mitigations or known hotfixes?
Ajay K: No active mitigations, only keepalive scripts. If the OOMs are on the model workers it's probably the new quantized 4-bit build. Last rollout was canary last night.
Lena P: I'm in EU timezone but awake. I can take secondary if needed. Will try to reach infra to increase node pool.
Samir B: I can be on the bridge for customer comms. Maria, do you want me to open a short status page?
Maria R: Yes please Samir. Quick check — diagnostics first: can we scale the model-worker ASG and roll back to previous image? Runbook link: https://runbooks/redwood/model-worker-oom
Maria R: Running suggested commands now:
```
# scale up workers briefly
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/model-worker --replicas=12
# rollback to previous stable image
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/model-worker model-worker=registry/redwood/model-worker:v1.18.3
```
incident-bot: Autoscaler triggered +3 nodes (provisioning). Estimated ready ~3m.
Lena P: If the rollback fails, we should set a routing policy to send traffic to cached-model variant (lower mem). That avoids user-visible errors while we fix the workers. Policy name: fallback_cached_model.
Maria R: Good call. Applying temporary routing:
```
# switch policy for route /generate to fallback_cached_model
curl -X POST https://api.redwood/internal/routing/switch -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/generate","policy":"fallback_cached_model"}'
```
Ajay K: Thanks. If you can get that in place and confirm reduced error rate I can authorise a canary abort from my phone.
Samir B: Status page: "Degraded generation in us-west-2; mitigation underway — fallback routing applied; next update in 10m" posted. Customers flagged: two paying enterprise orgs with active jobs, notified via DM.
Maria R: Confirming: after scaling + rollback + routing switch, errors dropped from 30% -> 4% over 2 minutes. Keeping monitoring on.
Lena P: I'll stay on secondary for the next 6 hours to cover the timezone overlap. If infra finishes node provisioning, consider reclaiming the scaled replicas to save cost once stable.
Ajay K: Appreciate you all. I'm leaving my phone on vibrate but will jump in if needed. Maria — please add a short incident summary to the ticket and mark me as delegated primary.
Maria R: Done — I updated the incident ticket with timeline, mitigations, customer impact, and followups (investigate quantized image memory regression, tighten canary checks). Marking Ajay as delegated.
Samir B: Closing loop with customers — sent a follow-up note to the two affected orgs and offered extra support window.
Maria R: Will hand back to Ajay when he's available, otherwise Lena will be primary for the remainder of the holiday. Logging postmortem tasks now. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Incident updated: severity downgraded to medium; still monitoring.
_meta: generated as a single slack thread string — messages are in chronological order and prefixed with sender names
